questions.prompt: Who is the Commander in Chief of the US armed forces?
choices: The Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff
questions.explanation: The Constitution makes the President the Commander in Chief. The chain of command then runs through the Secretary of Defense.

questions.prompt: Which of these is a civilian leader rather than a uniformed officer?
choices: Chief of Staff of the Air Force
Vice Chief of Staff of the Air Force
questions.explanation: The Secretary of the Air Force is a civilian who leads the Department of the Air Force. The Chief of Staff of the Air Force is the senior uniformed officer of the Air Force.

questions.prompt: Which military services are in the Department of the Air Force?
choices: The Air Force and Space Force
The Air Force and Air National Guard only
The Air Force and Coast Guard
questions.explanation: The Department of the Air Force includes both the US Air Force and the US Space Force.

questions.prompt: Who is the senior uniformed leader of the Space Force?
choices: The Space Force Chief of Staff
The Secretary of the Space Force
questions.explanation: The Chief of Space Operations is the Space Force's senior uniformed leader, alongside the Chief of Staff of the Air Force on the Joint Chiefs of Staff.

questions.prompt: Which list puts Air Force units in order from smallest to largest?
questions.explanation: Flight, squadron, group, wing. Above the wing come the numbered air force and the major command (MAJCOM).

questions.prompt: What is called the basic unit of the Air Force?
questions.explanation: The squadron is the basic unit of the Air Force, usually commanded by a Lieutenant Colonel or Major.

questions.prompt: Which major command (MAJCOM) is responsible for recruiting, training, and education, including Air University?
questions.explanation: Air Education and Training Command (AETC) handles recruiting, training, and education. Air University, which includes AFROTC, is part of AETC.

questions.prompt: Where is the headquarters of Air Force ROTC?
questions.explanation: AFROTC is run by the Jeanne M. Holm Center for Officer Accessions and Citizen Development at Maxwell AFB, Alabama, part of Air University.

questions.prompt: What title does the commander of an AFROTC detachment hold?
questions.explanation: The detachment commander is the Professor of Aerospace Studies (PAS), an active-duty officer, usually a Lieutenant Colonel or Colonel.

questions.prompt: In AFROTC, the first two years of Aerospace Studies (AS100 and AS200) are called:
questions.explanation: AS100 and AS200 make up the General Military Course (GMC). AS300 and AS400 make up the Professional Officer Course (POC).

questions.prompt: What must cadets usually complete to move from the General Military Course into the Professional Officer Course?
questions.explanation: Cadets attend Field Training, usually the summer after their AS200 year, before entering the POC.

questions.prompt: What is AFROTC's hands-on leadership training, held alongside academic classes, called?
questions.explanation: Leadership Laboratory (LLAB) is where cadets practice drill, customs and courtesies, and leadership, and where POC cadets lead the cadet wing.

questions.prompt: Who leads the cadet wing in an AFROTC detachment?
choices: A cadet wing commander, usually an AS400 cadet
questions.explanation: The cadet wing is led by cadets. The cadet wing commander is usually a senior (AS400) cadet, with POC cadets filling the cadet staff.

questions.prompt: Which of these AFOQT composite scores matters most for a pilot slot?
questions.explanation: Rated boards look closely at the Pilot composite, which is combined with flying hours and other factors into a pilot candidate score. Check current AFROTC guidance for minimums.
